title: bug: gemini mode runs the Gemini CLI with Antigravity's flags when agy is missing, treats agentCommand 'agy' as claude, and under MOE_RUNTIME_PROTECTED=1 resolves the Gemini CLI: both launchers run only Antigravity (agy), from MOE_AGY_COMMAND else PATH, with one fixed not-found message (PR #208 port, launcher slice)
definitionOfDone: Without MOE_RUNTIME_PROTECTED, both launchers run agy in gemini mode (MOE_WORKER_TYPE=GEMINI) for agentCommand `gemini` or `agy`: MOE_AGY_COMMAND when non-blank, else `agy` on PATH, never a `gemini` binary. With no agy both exit 1, run nothing and print `Antigravity CLI (agy) not found: <cmd>. Install Antigravity, or set MOE_AGY_COMMAND to the agy binary path (the IDE may not see your shell PATH).` Pinned by the 'gemini mode' rows of scripts/tests/protected-agent-command.test.mjs, passing on bash, PowerShell 7 and PowerShell 5.1.

Under MOE_RUNTIME_PROTECTED=1, `gemini` resolves and runs the trusted `agy` (`[INFO] MOE_PROTECTED_AGENT_CLI: agy -> <file>`), never the Gemini CLI or MOE_AGY_COMMAND. With no trusted agy it refuses with `MOE_PROTECTED_AGENT_CLI_NOT_FOUND: agy ...`, and agentCommand `agy` is refused with the unchanged MOE_PROTECTED_AGENT_COMMAND_REFUSED line. Pinned by the same rows.
scripts/tests/prompt-cache-launcher.test.mjs typeCases include `agy` and `C:/tools/agy.exe`, both exporting MOE_WORKER_TYPE=GEMINI, and pass.

parity-check.sh and parity-check.ps1 (pwsh 7 and PowerShell 5.1) require MOE_AGY_COMMAND and both not-found literals in both wrappers, and pass. npm run lint passes, and the plan's verification command passes fresh.

implementationPlan.description:
scripts/moe-agent.sh: three hunks, anchored by text. Each old block occurs once at edc3e937. Edit in place with the Edit tool and run `bash -n` afterwards. A task worktree needs no atomic-save dance (scripts/CLAUDE.md, worktree Launch bullet).
(a) CLI-type detection (~:639): 'elif [ "$CMD_BASE" = "gemini" ]; then' -> 'elif [ "$CMD_BASE" = "gemini" ] || [ "$CMD_BASE" = "agy" ]; then'. MOE_WORKER_TYPE then follows CLI_TYPE (GEMINI) with no further edit.
(b) The protected gate (~:955), inside `if [ "$RUNTIME_PROTECTED" = 1 ]; then`. Replace the line '    protected_resolve_cli "$COMMAND"' with two lines:
    # Gemini mode runs Antigravity only: the trusted lookup takes agy, never the Gemini CLI.
    if [ "$CLI_TYPE" = "gemini" ]; then protected_resolve_cli agy; else protected_resolve_cli "$COMMAND"; fi
CLI_TYPE is set at ~:634-644, earlier. The allowlist above (`case "$COMMAND" in claude|codex|gemini|grok`) is unchanged, so `agy` stays refused there.
(c) The gemini launch block (~:11612). Replace from '        if [ "$COMMAND_BIN" = "gemini" ] && command -v agy &> /dev/null; then' through the not-found check's `exit 1` / `fi` with:
        # Gemini mode runs Antigravity (agy) only, never the Gemini CLI, which rejects agy's flags.
        # MOE_AGY_COMMAND names agy when the IDE's PATH lacks it; a blank value counts as unset.
        # Under the protected marker COMMAND_BIN is already the trusted agy (protected_resolve_cli).
        if [ "$RUNTIME_PROTECTED" != 1 ]; then
            GEMINI_BIN_BASE=$(basename "$COMMAND_BIN")
            case "${MOE_AGY_COMMAND:-}" in
                *[![:space:]]*) COMMAND_BIN="$MOE_AGY_COMMAND" ;;
                *) if [ "${GEMINI_BIN_BASE%.*}" = "gemini" ]; then COMMAND_BIN="agy"; fi ;;
            esac
        fi
        if ! command -v "$COMMAND_BIN" &> /dev/null; then
            echo -e "${RED}[ERROR]${NC} Antigravity CLI (agy) not found: $COMMAND_BIN. Install Antigravity, or set MOE_AGY_COMMAND to the agy binary path (the IDE may not see your shell PATH)."
            exit 1
        fi
Why `case` and not `-n`: the architect's dry run showed `-n "${MOE_AGY_COMMAND:-}"` runs a whitespace-only value as the command ('not found:  .'), while ps1's IsNullOrWhiteSpace treats it as unset. Row AG2 pins the shared behaviour. `${MOE_AGY_COMMAND:-}` keeps `set -u` safe. The pattern parses on macOS /bin/bash 3.2. COMMAND_ARGV, the command's own arguments, is kept. Error handling: a missing agy exits 1 before GEMINI.md is written and before any CLI or heartbeat starts, as today.

Parity needles, placed after CQ-M07s's landed lines (governor comment-8c983720). s added the families at ~:41-46 and the 'check dispatch' loop at ~:163-167 in the sh, and the dynamicPatterns at ~:41-45 and the 'check dispatch' group at ~:118-120 in the ps1. Neither new block is adjacent to them.
- scripts/tests/parity-check.sh: directly after the grok banner loop ('  require_both "grok banner" "$banner"' / 'done'), add:
# Gemini mode runs Antigravity (agy) only: both wrappers read MOE_AGY_COMMAND and
# stop with the same not-found message, never a fallback to the Gemini CLI.
for agy_lit in MOE_AGY_COMMAND 'Antigravity CLI (agy) not found:' \
  'Install Antigravity, or set MOE_AGY_COMMAND to the agy binary path (the IDE may not see your shell PATH).'; do
  require_both "gemini mode (Antigravity)" "$agy_lit"
done
- scripts/tests/parity-check.ps1: as the LAST entry of the `$required = [ordered]@{` table, after the 'Serena TOOL-tier tools' group and before its closing '}', add:
    # Gemini mode runs Antigravity (agy) only: both wrappers read MOE_AGY_COMMAND
    # and stop with the same not-found message, never a fallback to the Gemini CLI.
    'gemini mode (Antigravity)' = @('MOE_AGY_COMMAND', 'Antigravity CLI (agy) not found:', 'Install Antigravity, or set MOE_AGY_COMMAND to the agy binary path (the IDE may not see your shell PATH).')
parity-check.ps1 has no BOM, so the added text must stay ASCII (no em-dash). Dry run: with the needles and the old wrappers, parity-check.sh reported 3 'gemini mode (Antigravity) ... missing from: moe-agent.sh moe-agent.ps1' failures; with steps 1-2 both scripts PASS, the ps1 on pwsh 7 and on 5.1.

Verification, run ONCE after steps 1-4, from this task's worktree root. The command is the 3 executionContract.checkRefs joined with ' && ', in order:
- the 'gemini mode' rows on WSL node (bash) and on Windows node.exe (PowerShell 5.1 and pwsh 7), in parallel;
- the agy typeCases on both nodes, in parallel;
- bash -n, parity-check.sh and npm run lint, then ParseFile of moe-agent.ps1 and parity-check.ps1 on pwsh.exe and on powershell.exe.
Its fresh output is the complete_task evidence. Expect:
- 'gemini mode rows: rc=0 bash=8 ps51=8 ps7=8' (8 or more each);
- 'agy type rows: rc=0 linux=2 windows=6' (or more);

The architect's dry run took about 50 s for the rows plus 6 s for the rest. That fits the human's 20-minute gate rail; per that rail and comment-1a9850e2, do not run postflight.sh or postflight.ps1, and no JetBrains test (no Kotlin changes here). Linux pwsh is optional: on WSL its rows skip, and the gate counts bash there.
Error handling for a red run:
- A red row prints its log path: read the TAP 'not ok' block, which carries the wrapper's stdout and stderr.
- 'a CLI ran' or a wrong ran.log line means the remap or protected resolution is off.
- A count below 8 with rc=0 means a row skipped: the engine is missing, so check pwsh.exe and powershell.exe on the WSL PATH (mem:gotcha-pwsh7-reachable-from-wsl).
- Never weaken a row or the count.
- WSL leaks MOE_* into Windows processes: the pieces unset every MOE_*/CLAUDE* variable (mem:gotcha-launcher-ps1-rows-from-wsl).

comments.author: architect-2a219562
comments.content:
Verification trap, found by architect-2a219562 while planning task-ff0df867 (proof run in bash). The verify step joins the 3 checkRefs with ' && ', but each ref is a `;`-sequence. `&&` links only one ref's last command to the next ref's `cd`, so the rest of the next ref runs anyway and the exit code is the LAST ref's alone. A red "gemini mode rows" ref followed by green parity/lint therefore returns 0. Proof: `bash -c 'echo "ref0 says FAIL"; false && cd /; echo "ref1 body ran"; true'` returns 0.
Fix, with no ref byte changed: wrap each ref in a subshell, `( <ref0> ) && ( <ref1> ) && ( <ref2> )`. The chain then stops at the first red ref and returns its code.

executionContract.intendedBehavior: Gemini mode always runs Antigravity (agy) and never the Gemini CLI, in both launchers. agentCommand `gemini` or `agy` (base name without extension, any path) selects gemini mode (MOE_WORKER_TYPE=GEMINI). Without MOE_RUNTIME_PROTECTED=1 the binary is a non-blank MOE_AGY_COMMAND, else `agy` in place of a `gemini` command, else the given command, with its arguments kept. When it is not found, both launchers exit 1 before any CLI starts and print `Antigravity CLI (agy) not found: <cmd>. Install Antigravity, or set MOE_AGY_COMMAND to the agy binary path (the IDE may not see your shell PATH).` Under MOE_RUNTIME_PROTECTED=1 the four-name allowlist is unchanged, so `agy` is refused. For `gemini` the trusted lookup resolves `agy` (INFO `MOE_PROTECTED_AGENT_CLI: agy -> <file>`), MOE_AGY_COMMAND is not read, and a missing trusted agy refuses with MOE_PROTECTED_AGENT_CLI_NOT_FOUND naming agy. parity-check.sh and parity-check.ps1 require the shared literals.

bash -n and ParseFile (both engines) are clean, and npm run lint passes.
invariants: Gemini mode never execs a binary whose base name is gemini.
Under MOE_RUNTIME_PROTECTED=1 the CLI that runs is the one the trusted lookup resolved (an absolute PATH entry outside the project), never an env-provided path.
postflight-vm-route.{sh,ps1} and .moe/ are untouched. CQ-M07s's parity lines stay as landed, and the new blocks are not adjacent to them.

The protected allowlist and its refusal line are unchanged (byte-identical in both wrappers), and JetBrains PROTECTED_AGENT_COMMANDS needs no change.

Other CLIs (claude, codex, grok, custom) and their branches are unchanged. The gemini block's argv (--print / --prompt-interactive), the GEMINI.md and settings.json writers, and the banners are unchanged.

checkRefs: cd "$(git rev-parse --show-toplevel)"; U=$(env | grep -oE '^(MOE_|CLAUDE)[A-Z0-9_]*' | sed 's/^/-u /'); F=scripts/tests/protected-agent-command.test.mjs; L=$(mktemp); N=$(mktemp); (env $U node --test --test-reporter=tap --test-name-pattern 'gemini mode' $F > $L 2>&1) & a=$!; (env $U "/mnt/c/Program Files/nodejs/node.exe" --test --test-reporter=tap --test-name-pattern 'gemini mode' $F > $N 2>&1) & b=$!; r=0; wait $a || r=1; wait $b || r=1; k(){ tr -d '\r' < "$1" | grep -E "^ok [0-9]+ - $2: [^#]*gemini mode" | grep -vc '# SKIP'; }; s="bash=$(k $L bash) ps51=$(k $N 'PowerShell 5.1') ps7=$(k $N 'PowerShell 7')"; echo "gemini mode rows: rc=$r $s (logs $L $N)"; [ $r = 0 ] && echo "$s" | grep -qE '^bash=([89]|[1-9][0-9]) ps51=([89]|[1-9][0-9]) ps7=([89]|[1-9][0-9])$'

cd "$(git rev-parse --show-toplevel)"; U=$(env | grep -oE '^(MOE_|CLAUDE)[A-Z0-9_]*' | sed 's/^/-u /'); F=scripts/tests/prompt-cache-launcher.test.mjs; L=$(mktemp); N=$(mktemp); (env $U node --test --test-reporter=tap --test-name-pattern MOE_WORKER_TYPE $F > $L 2>&1) & a=$!; (env $U "/mnt/c/Program Files/nodejs/node.exe" --test --test-reporter=tap --test-name-pattern MOE_WORKER_TYPE $F > $N 2>&1) & b=$!; r=0; wait $a || r=1; wait $b || r=1; k(){ tr -d '\r' < "$1" | grep -E '^ok [0-9]+ - [^#]*: (C:/tools/)?agy(\.exe)? exports MOE_WORKER_TYPE=GEMINI' | grep -vc '# SKIP'; }; echo "agy type rows: rc=$r linux=$(k $L) windows=$(k $N) (logs $L $N)"; [ $r = 0 ] && [ "$(k $L)" -ge 2 ] && [ "$(k $N)" -ge 6 ]

cd "$(git rev-parse --show-toplevel)"; P=$(wslpath -w "$PWD"); bash -n scripts/moe-agent.sh && bash scripts/tests/parity-check.sh && npm run lint --silent && for e in pwsh.exe powershell.exe; do $e -NoProfile -Command "\$x=\$null;[void][Management.Automation.Language.Parser]::ParseFile('$P\scripts\moe-agent.ps1',[ref]\$null,[ref]\$x);if(\$x.Count){\$x;exit 1};'ParseFile ok'" && $e -NoProfile -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File "$P\scripts\tests\parity-check.ps1" || exit 1; done

planningNotes.approachesConsidered:
- A literal #208 port (remap only in the gemini block) was rejected for the protected runtime. protected_resolve_cli and Resolve-MoeProtectedCli resolve the command NAME first, so a protected gemini seat would still require the Gemini CLI to be installed, refuse when only agy exists, and then run a bare `agy` or an env-provided MOE_AGY_COMMAND that the trusted lookup never vetted. Instead, the trusted lookup takes agy for gemini and the block skips the remap under the marker.
- Adding `agy` to the protected allowlist was rejected. The refusal line is byte-identical across the wrappers, the tests pin it, and JetBrains PROTECTED_AGENT_COMMANDS has the same four names (task-aa85ff13). Under protection gemini reaches agy anyway.
- ps1 Write-Error (as in #208) was replaced by [Console]::Error.WriteLine, because EAP 'Stop' turns Write-Error into a throw (:128's comment documents the same pattern).
- Whitespace-only MOE_AGY_COMMAND is blank in both launchers. The dry run caught a `-n` sh sketch diverging from ps1's IsNullOrWhiteSpace.
- A new test file plus ci.yml wiring was rejected for the file count. protected-agent-command.test.mjs already is the whole-launcher harness for agentCommand. CI coverage of the detection comes through prompt-cache-launcher's typeCases (all three OSes).
planningNotes.codebaseInsights:
- A governor seat with the inert runtime stub reaches the gemini launch block in about 0.6 s on bash and about 2 s on pwsh. That made whole-launcher rows cheap (32-36 s for 8 rows x 2 engines per node).
- Under the marker the sh PATH is scrubbed and COMMAND_BIN is the absolute trusted path; command -v on it succeeds.
- The ps1 resolves the protected CLI BEFORE type detection (:649 vs :1227), so 2(a) tests $Command and 2(b) must accept agy, or a protected seat would detect claude.
- CQ-M07s landed after the original claim (edc3e937). The ps1 gemini block moved from ~:10993 to ~:11136; all anchors still occur once.
- Stub .cmd files on Windows echo %MOE_WORKER_TYPE%, which proves detection without logging argv (prompt quotes would break cmd echo).

This row runs in parallel with CQ-M07t (task-527735ea, re-planning; receipt/journal code, far from these hunks) and task-e444f6ae (ps1 check-dispatch stop area ~:9575-9640, about 1500 lines away). merge-tree lands disjoint hunks; a true conflict takes the LANDING-CONFLICT resume.
